away.name: Anthony Stolarz
away.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has played poorly, so Stolarz will return to the crease on Friday for the fifth time in six games. The 32-year-old Stolarz played well in his most recent game, helping the Maple Leafs snap a miserable nine-game losing streak (0-8-1), saving 20 of 22 shots (.909 SV%) in a 4-2 win over the New York Islanders. The Maple Leafs enter Friday's game as +146 road underdogs against the Boston Bruins, who have scored two or fewer goals in four of their past six games (2-4-0).

home.name: Jeremy Swayman
home.news: Swayman had a tremendous start to the 2026-27 season, posting a stellar 1.85 GAA and .934 SV% in his first seven games (6-1-0). That said, the 28-year-old American goalie has battled some adversity in the weeks since, posting a subpar 3.22 GAA and .879 SV% in his last 10 games (5-5-1). The Bruins enter Friday's game as -148 home favourites against a Toronto Maple Leafs team coming off a 4-2 win over the New York Islanders.

away.name: Devin Cooley
away.news: Cooley was playing the best hockey of his NHL career before suffering a lower-body injury that sidelined him for over a week in late October. That said, Dustin Wolf has played better since then, taking the reins in the Calgary crease, but Cooley is coming off a solid outing, despite a 2-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators, saving 29 of 31 shots (.935 SV%). That said, the Flames enter Friday's game as sizeable +205 road underdogs against the New Jersey Devils.

home.name: Jake Allen
home.news: Jake Allen was relied upon heavily by the Devils to start the 2026-27 season, but since the acquisition of Connor Hellebuyck, Allen hasn't played much. The 36-year-old Allen last played on November 21st, relieving Hellebuyck and allowing four goals on 16 shots (.750 SV%) in a 9-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues. Since Hellebuyck joined the Devils, Allen has a 4.17 GAA and .852 SV% in four games (1-3-0). Still, the Devils enter Friday's matinée as sizeable -242 home favourites against the Calgary Flames, who snapped a three-game losing streak on Wednesday with a 6-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins.

away.name: Karel Vejmelka
away.news: The Mammoth have alternated goalies in recent weeks, hoping one of Karel Vejmelka or Sebastian Cossa can take the reins. Still, neither has been able to perform consistently. The 30-year-old Vejmelka wasn't spectacular in his previous game, but he secured a 4-3 win over the Minnesota Wild, saving 22 of 25 shots (.880 SV%). The win snapped a six-game losing streak for Vejmelka (0-4-2). Utah enters Friday's game as -114 road favourites against the Nashville Predators.

home.name: Juuse Saros
home.news: Saros narrowly missed out on a shutout in his previous game, allowing a goal in the final minute of a 20-save performance (.952 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the Dallas Stars. After a couple of concerning seasons, the 31-year-old Finnish goalie seems to have returned to elite form. He has a stellar 1.71 GAA and .940 SV% in his last eight games (6-2-0).

away.name: Casey DeSmith
away.news: DeSmith won a career-high 15 games last season and emerged as one of the NHL's most reliable backup goalies, but he has been used sparingly to start the 2026-27 season. That said, the 35-year-old DeSmith was stellar in his most recent outing, saving 25 of 26 shots (.962 SV%) in a 2-1 overtime win over the Florida Panthers. The Stars enter Friday's game as -131 road favourites against the St. Louis Blues.

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer has emerged as the undisputed number-one goalie in St. Louis and has been consistent on most nights. He was solid in his most recent outing, saving 27 of 29 shots (.931 SV%) in a 3-2 shootout loss to the New York Islanders. The 26-year-old goalie has had an outstanding November, posting a 2.20 GAA and .925 SV% in eight games (4-3-1). The Blues enter Friday's game as +111 home underdogs against the Dallas Stars.

away.name: Linus Ullmark
away.news: Ullmark will start in Tampa Bay on Friday.

away.name: Jacob Markstrom
away.news: Markstrom hasn't had to be spectacular this season, but he has done enough on most nights to help his team secure victories. The 36-year-old Swedish goalie allowed three goals on 28 shots (.893 SV%) in his most recent game, a 5-3 win over the Ottawa Senators. He has allowed three or more goals in nine of 14 games this season, but still has a solid 8-4-1 record. The Panthers enter Friday's game as -108 road favourites against the Washington Capitals.

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Over the past two seasons, Thompson quietly became one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. That said, the 29-year-old goalie has been flat-out unreliable through the quarter-mark of the 2026-27 season. In 16 games this season (8-6-0), Thompson has allowed three or more goals 11 times. The Capitals enter Friday's game as slight -101 home underdogs against the Florida Panthers.

home.name: Jet Greaves
home.news: Greaves hasn't played much in recent weeks, but will return to the crease on Friday. The 25-year-old Greaves had a tremendous first full NHL season in 2025-26, posting a 2.60 GAA and .908 SV% in 55 games (26-19-9), but hasn't had that same success in 2026-27. Greaves has lost eight of 10 starts this season (2-8-0) while allowing a concerning three or more goals eight times. The Blue Jackets enter Friday's game as -125 home favourites against a Detroit Red Wings team coming off a 5-1 win over the Vancouver Canucks.

home.name: Laurent Brossoit
home.news: Brossoit had a successful stint with the Ducks earlier this month, but was surprisingly sent down to San Diego (AHL) after a 4-2 loss to the Nashville Predators on November 11th, when he allowed four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%). In his return to action on Wednesday, Brossoit made a strong case for staying in the NHL, recording the Ducks' first shutout of the season with 23 saves in a 7-0 win over the San Jose Sharks. The Ducks enter Friday's game as slight -104 home underdogs against the Los Angeles Kings, who are coming off a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens.

home.name: Semyon Varlamov
home.news: After missing the entire 2025-26 season due to an injury, Varlamov's return to the crease in 2026-27 has been inconsistent. The veteran 38-year-old goalie struggled in his most recent outing, allowing four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Winnipeg Jets. That said, he has helped his team record a point in six of his last seven games (2-1-3). The Islanders enter Friday's game as -117 home favourites in a rematch against the Jets, who are 9-1-1 in their past 11 games.

away.name: Sergei Murashov
away.news: The Penguins are having a miserable season, but the lightly used Murashov has shown some encouraging signs between the pipes. The 22-year-old rookie goalie had a poor outing, allowing four goals on 29 shots (.862 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the Nashville Predators. The loss ended a solid three-game stretch for Murashov (2-1-0), in which he saved 91 of 98 shots (.929 SV%). The Penguins enter Friday's game as +126 road underdogs against the Buffalo Sabres.

home.name: Tristan Jarry
home.news: After a disappointing introduction to the Oilers in the 2025-26 season, Jarry has been reliable on most nights in 2026-27. That said, he struggled in his most recent game, allowing four goals on 27 shots (.852 SV%) in a 5-4 shootout loss to the St. Louis Blues. It snapped a six-game stretch in which Jarry allowed three or fewer goals in each game (4-0-2). The Oilers enter Friday's outing as -203 home favourites against the Seattle Kraken, who are coming off a 3-1 loss to the Chicago Blackhawks.
